prompt: Built for learning how an EOS M 290 laser powder bed fusion metal 3D printer works: a cut-away of the machine building a twisted turbine blade, with the scanner head open so the galvo mirrors can be seen steering the beam, where laser power, scan speed and hatch distance set the melt pool, the scan tracks and the porosity of the part.
